title: Never learned to read music; chords only
summary: Never read music; he studied the chord system and a chord book, practices chords only, and wants more playing with others.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I was wondering, did you ever learn to read music on the piano or the guitar?
Well, no, I'm going to be straight with you. I never did learn to read the music. I played, but you know what I mean, I never worried about music on a compliment, you see what I mean?
A lot of people were that great, like you said, but Mel San Diego couldn't read it all.
No, you know what I studied the whole lot was the chord system, you know? I studied the chord form. If you played in B-flat, well you know you'd have to make F, B-flat, you'd have to make E-flat.
You knew all those chords then.

I learned the chords. I never learned the music. I just learned the chords. I mean I learned them on the piano. I bought me a chord, you know, a book. Yes. And I made the chords and learned how to play them when I get rid of the band, while if I fumble on the number, well I'll try to catch it, you know what I mean, the best I can.
A lot of people learn that way very well.

And then about me practicing and that's all I do, just when I get on the piano right now I just practice chords. I don't practice no melody. But I like to learn how to play the melody on the banjo, that's what I like.

Yeah, like George. Well of course I play one or two pieces and everything. The trouble is with my playing now that I don't work out with nobody. I should be working out with somebody, you know what I mean, to get the right time, you know.
